messages.author: fd400f07a4fde015
messages.subject: Run script from part 3
parts:
Dear all,

Based  on this sentence in the vignette "The reason why it split up in parts is that it avoids having the re-do all analysis if you only want to make a small change in the more downstream parts", I was wondering if there is a straightforward method to initiate the GGIR script from part 3? I'm interested in testing a different sleep algorithm and it would save significant time if I could skip rerunning from part 1. Currently, I've come across a GitHub with functions g.part3, g.part4, and g.part5, but they seem complex to me.

Thank you for your assistance.

Kind regards,

Marga

messages.author: 5270e62a7d3ec577
messages.subject: Re: Run script from part 3
parts:
Hi Marga,

Yes you can do this. There are some unnecessary steps here but this is what I was doing if I was wanting to re-run parts 3 and 4 to generate a new report with different thresholds for sleep:
1. Copy the part4 results elsewhere.
2. delete config.csv file in output_x
3. Delete ms3.out and ms4.out folders in the output_x/meta folder (leave basic, ms1.out, ms2..out folders)
4. Delete part4 output files in output_x/results folder.
5. change GGIR script to mode=c(3,4) and do.report=c(4), and overwrite=T, then any other functions you want to change e.g. anglethreshold, timethreshold for different parameters.
6. re-run the GGIR script.
7. new meta files and results will be generated based on the newer parameters.

The majority (if not all) of the above isn't necessary if you just include overwrite = TRUE in the GGIR call,  so most of the steps described are just how I do it to make sure that anything I don't want overwriting is copied elsewhere before inadvertently replacing it and having to re-generate.

Thanks,
Ben

messages.subject: Re: Run script from part 3
parts:
Hi Ben,

Thank you for your response!
I tried to do what you said, but I don't get results. 

You think a script like the following should work? Did I miss something in the script?
GGIR(
  mode=c(3,4,5),
  datadir="D:/GGIR/Input",
  outputdir="D:/GGIR/Output",
  overwrite = TRUE,
  do.parallel = TRUE,
  desiredtz="Europe/Brussels",
  do.report=c(3,4,5),
  do.visual = TRUE,
  loglocation="D:/GGIR/Input/Sleeplogv2.csv",
  sleeplogidnum = FALSE, 
  colid = 1, 
  coln1 = 3, 
  
  
  HASIB.algo="Sadeh1994",
  Sadeh_axis="Y",
  sensor.location="hip",
  HASPT.algo="HorAngle",
  longitudinal_axis=2, #Only used when sensor.location = “hip” or HASPT.algo = “HorAngle”
  timethreshold=(5),#default
  anglethreshold=5,#default
  ignorenonwear=TRUE,
  excludefirst.part4=TRUE,
  def.noc.sleep=1,
  do.sibreport=TRUE,
  possible_nap_edge_acc=Inf,
  possible_nap_dur = c(15, 240),
  #=====================
  # Part 5 
  #=====================
  threshold.lig = 26, threshold.mod = 420, threshold.vig = 842,
  boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
  boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
  boutdur.mvpa = c(1),
  includedaycrit.part5 = 2/3, 
  
  #=====================
  # Visual report
  #=====================
  timewindow = c("WW"), 
  visualreport=TRUE,
  week_weekend_aggregate.part5 = TRUE)


Thank you for the assistance! 

Kind regards,
Marga
